question.text: The Kaveri Macro Fund uses a PARALLEL structure: a domestic AIF in India and an offshore fund in Mauritius invest alongside each other in the same investee companies. Which statement is CORRECT about a parallel structure?

answer.text: Only the domestic AIF invests; the offshore fund only advises
Two separate pooling vehicles in different jurisdictions invest independently into the same investee universe; each has its own manager and fee structure
Both vehicles pool into a common master fund
The offshore fund invests in the domestic AIF which then invests in the investees

explanation.text: The Logic: Parallel structure uses TWO separate pooling vehicles (onshore AIF + offshore fund), each with its own manager and investor base, both investing directly into the SAME investee universe in parallel. No cross-investment between the two. Each fund earns its own fees — which makes parallel typically costlier than master-feeder. The Trap: Option C describes master-feeder (single master). Option D describes master-feeder with the AIF as master. Only B captures parallel. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D cover the same structural taxonomy. XIX-B distributors must explain parallel vs feeder to HNI clients. Manager's Pro-Tip: In parallel, you may face pro-rata allocation questions (domestic vs offshore pool getting the same investee share). Document allocation policy in your IMA/offshore-fund IMA to avoid disputes at IPO lock-up or in partial fills.
